content.title: About
content.content: Cookies, Puerto Rican style are a traditional sweet treat made from wheat flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and flavored with cinnamon, cloves, and ground allspice. The dough is rolled into small round discs and baked until golden. They are often enjoyed with tea or coffee and are a staple at festive gatherings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In Puerto Rico these cookies are commonly called “polvorones,” which translates to “little crumbs.”
The recipe frequently uses “masacho,” a local cane sugar that gives a distinct caramel note.
Cookies are sometimes dusted with powdered sugar or glazed to mimic the intricate patterns of Puerto Rican pottery.
Some regional variations add raisins or shredded coconut, reflecting Caribbean influences.
They are baked in large batches for family celebrations such as Saint Joseph’s Day and Christmas.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates in the cookies provide quick energy, making them a handy snack before work or study.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Flour and cane sugar contribute a modest amount of iron, supporting blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and butter add vitamins B1, B2, and B6, which aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Cinnamon and cloves are rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: Butter supplies monounsaturated fats, which in moderate amounts can be heart‑friendly.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The cookies contain wheat flour, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Butter may cause discomfort for those who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, the cookies are calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookies can be enjoyed on their own, paired with hot coffee, tea, or hot chocolate. They also serve as a base for layered cakes, placed between cream layers, or crumbled over ice cream for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container at room temperature in a dry place. They can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week, or frozen for longer storage, retaining flavor for up to three months.
